name: Tusi Sites
description: In the mountains of south-west China, the Tusi Sites preserve the remains of three hilltop strongholds: Laosicheng, Tangya and Hailongtun Fortress. Each was home to a local chief whom the emperor appointed as a hereditary ruler, a system that lasted from the 13th to the early 20th century. It let minority peoples keep their own customs while remaining part of the empire.
